title: Catalog Opening
event: Across the familiar Kaufhaus atrium, rows of fixtures click into a new operational rhythm: tall shelving bay fronts fold like ledger pages, pneumatic shutters slide forward in a metronome, and identical wooden crates roll out from beneath display plinths into a precise, catalogue-like queue down the central aisle.
consequence: A tidy line of identical wooden crates sits in the central aisle, their lids slightly ajar, leaving a stamped wooden edge pattern across the tile.
nextHook: The crate line leads into the refrigerated island where the next set of displays will be revealed.
stillPrompt: Interior of a real Kaufhaus atrium reconfigured into a mechanical catalogue: shelving faces folded into regular ledger panels, pneumatic shutters halfway closed, and a neat trail of identical wooden crates laid out down the main aisle. Strong overhead architecture, tiled floor, cold display cases in the background; no people visible.
videoPrompt: Slow five-second crane pull back from ground level: shutters snap in their rhythm, crates roll precisely into a single file down the tiled central aisle beneath the atrium's skylights; sound of pneumatic breaths and wooden thuds. Keep the real Kaufhaus architecture recognizable — columns, mezzanine railing, tiled floor — no text or logos, no monster.
cameraCue: Crane starts low at crate edge, rises and pulls back to reveal full aisle and folded shelving rhythm.

title: Butchered Inventory
event: Crates along the aisle snap open like drawers and their trays present fleshy, tray-packed forms — dense, waxed slabs arranged on chilled plates inside the refrigerated island. Condensation blooms across glass fronts; mannequins are swapped for lined stainless trays. Staff step back as moisture beads and a dark, rust-colored smear drips onto the tile.
consequence: A dark, blood-like smear arcs across the tile from the refrigerated island and pools toward an adjacent aisle.
nextHook: The smear trail leads into the next refrigerated gap where brittle safety plates begin to appear and will interact with whatever rises.
stillPrompt: Close-up on opened wooden crates inside the Kaufhaus refrigerated island: trays of dense, waxed slabs on chilled stainless, cold fog on glass, and a dark smear beginning to drip onto the floor. Industrial lighting highlights moisture and texture; no people, no monster.
videoPrompt: Two-second push-in: crate lids bang open, frosted breath fogs and beads on the glass, waxed slabs on trays wobble then settle as a dark smear runs off a tray onto the tile; staff shadow at periphery recoiling. Maintain real store fixtures and lighting; do not show the monster.
cameraCue: Handheld macro push toward the smear as it drips off the tray onto the tile.

title: Labels Rise
event: Brittle, thin plates—like hammered safety placards—crackle out of instrument cases stacked among the trays. From the narrow gap between two stacked refrigerated crates, a weathered practical sculpture lifts itself up: a human-scale assemblage of worn mannequin parts, butcher's paper, rusting metal brackets and those brittle plates adhered to its skin. It peels one plate free; each removed plate fractures with a white puff of powder and a tiny metallic ring.
consequence: A scatter of cracked brittle plates and white powder dust lies across the floor around the crate gap.
nextHook: The brittle plates spread into the public aisle and will be swept up by staff and encountered by shoppers, provoking a crowd reaction.
stillPrompt: A weathered practical sculpture stands half-emerged from stacked refrigerated crates in the Kaufhaus: patched mannequin limbs, butcher's paper wrapping, rusted metal brackets, and brittle, hammered plates adhered across its torso. The object is clearly a filmed prop, tactile and weathered; fractured plates lie at its feet.
videoPrompt: Three-second low dolly then quick overhead: camera approaches the crate gap as a practical sculpture rises — its skin a collage of butcher's paper and brittle safety plates — it peels one plate and a puff of white powder fractures into air. Emphasize tactile materials (paper, metal, wax) and the real store environment; capture physical sound of plates cracking.
cameraCue: Low-angle dolly in to the sculpture rising, then cut to a fast overhead to show scattered plates on the floor.

title: Crowd Reflex
event: Shoppers converge on the aisle where the brittle plates lie. Sales staff form a human chain to sweep and collect fragments; a shopper trips on a cracked plate and a glass display tumbles, shattering at the base of an escalator. The ripple of bodies and a dropped bag wedge against a security sensor, causing a tensioned door to shudder.
consequence: A smashed glass display and a bag jammed against a security door sensor; the door begins to stutter under pressure.
nextHook: The jammed sensor and human pressure will trigger the security system to slam and seal zones, forming an inner chamber in the next scene.
stillPrompt: Crowd scene inside the Kaufhaus: shoppers and staff clustered in an aisle, people sweeping brittle plate fragments into boxes, a shattered glass display at the base of an escalator and a bag caught in a sensor; expressions of alarm and urgency, no monster shown.
videoPrompt: Two-second handheld through the crowd: staff sweeping, a shopper stumbling and glass shattering, a bag wedging against a sensor as people push; tension builds with quick cuts between hands, feet, and the jammed bag. Keep the real interior and people filmic; do not show the sculpture.
cameraCue: Handheld weave through shoppers, then whip to the jammed bag and stuttering security door.

title: Encircled
event: The jammed sensor and human pressure trip the store's fail-safe: heavy security shutters slam down and a ring of automatic doors close, isolating a central chamber. Panic compresses into a human press at the glass. Inside the sealed zone the same weathered practical sculpture paces, pressing a brittle plate to the frosted glass; fluorescent lights strobe in fractured intervals while the crowd outside presses palms to the opaque surface.
consequence: A sealed inner chamber behind frosted glass with the sculpture visible inside; dents and a fresh gouge mark the tiled floor where the shutters hit.
nextHook: When the doors are later reopened, the sealed contents and the damaged floor will be repurposed for commerce — the plates and fragments will be sold as objects.
stillPrompt: Frosted security glass and slammed metal shutters inside the Kaufhaus form a sealed inner chamber; behind the glass a weathered practical sculpture presses a brittle plate to the window, lit by strobing fluorescents. Outside, pressed hands and scattered bags, and a dented tile where a shutter hit.
videoPrompt: Five-second overhead crane then slow descent: doors slam into place, lights strobe, the camera reveals the sealed chamber and the sculpture pacing inside pressing plates to the glass while the crowd outside pounds the pane. Capture real store architecture, shutter mechanics, and the tactile prop; do not include any readable text.
cameraCue: Overhead crane drop to reveal the sealed chamber, then slow descent to a low angle on the dented tile.

title: Merchandise of Panic
event: After the shutters are eased, staff reconfigure the sealed zone into a temporary checkout: brittle plates and fractured fragments are sorted onto a carousel and passed beneath a blank imprinting press that stamps round tokens. Conveyor belts carry the plates behind plexiglass as curious shoppers queue and accept blank stamped tokens — the residue of alarm becomes a purchasable souvenir.
consequence: A carousel of brittle plates behind plexiglass and shoppers holding blank stamped tokens; aisles rearranged into token kiosks.
nextHook: The Kaufhaus returns to commercial order with panic recycled into commodities; the original conflict remains visible in the shelved plates and the dented tile.
stillPrompt: Quiet aftermath inside the Kaufhaus: a plexiglass carousel displays brittle plates once scattered in the aisles, a small imprinting press stamping blank round tokens, and shoppers carrying the new tokens as they move through reconfigured aisles. The dented tile from the shutters is visible in the foreground; no sculpture shown.
videoPrompt: Two-second conveyor-close: belt moves brittle plates under a stamping press, close on a palm receiving a blank stamped token then pull back to show the carousel behind plexiglass and shoppers browsing. Emphasize tactile surfaces and the repurposed store systems; do not show the sculpture or any readable text.
cameraCue: Tight push-in to the imprinting press on the conveyor, then pull back to reveal the carousel and shoppers.
